questions.q: Besides protecting the nucleic acid, the capsid of a naked virus also:
o: Helps the virus attach to receptors on the host cell
Carries out respiration for the virus
questions.x: The capsid shields the genome and, in non-enveloped viruses, carries the proteins that bind host receptors. Viruses have no metabolism, so they make no ATP and no proteins on their own.

questions.q: Among injecting drug users, the most direct way to prevent the spread of HIV is to:
o: Inject only into muscles, not veins
Wash the syringe with cold water between users
Use a new sterile syringe and needle for every injection
questions.x: HIV passes in traces of blood left in shared needles and syringes, so a fresh sterile set for each injection stops this route. Antibiotics do not act on viruses, and cold-water rinsing does not remove infected blood.

questions.q: Excess glucose eaten beyond the body's needs can be turned into fatty acids for storage. This conversion takes place through the intermediate:
questions.x: Glucose is broken down to pyruvate and then acetyl CoA; acetyl CoA units can be joined to build fatty acids. This is why acetyl CoA links carbohydrate and fat metabolism.

questions.q: When a person loses body fat by dieting and exercise, most of the mass of the fat leaves the body as:
questions.x: Fat is oxidized completely to carbon dioxide, which is breathed out, and water. Urea comes from proteins, not fats.

questions.q: During long starvation, the usual order in which the body draws on its fuel reserves is:
o: Protein first, then fat, then carbohydrate
Fat first, then protein, then carbohydrate
All three equally from the start
Carbohydrate (glycogen) first, then fat, and protein last
questions.x: Glycogen stores are used first and last only about a day; fat then becomes the main fuel. Body protein is broken down in large amounts only when fat runs low.

questions.q: Which bond is NOT involved in holding the tertiary structure of a protein?
questions.x: Tertiary structure is held by hydrogen bonds, ionic bonds, disulphide bridges and hydrophobic interactions between R groups. Glycosidic bonds link sugars, not amino acids.

questions.q: The strand 5′-AGC-3′ is paired with its complementary strand. How many hydrogen bonds hold this short segment together?
questions.x: The pairs are A–T (2 hydrogen bonds), G–C (3) and C–G (3), giving 2 + 3 + 3 = 8.

questions.q: In the amino acid alanine, the R group is:
questions.x: Alanine's side chain is –CH₃. The R group –H belongs to glycine, –CH₂SH to cysteine and –CH₂COOH to aspartic acid.

questions.q: Which shows the correct order from smallest to largest?
questions.x: A codon is three nucleotides, a gene is a long sequence of codons, and a chromosome carries many genes.

questions.q: Malt sugar (maltose) is produced in large amounts in:
o: Cellulose cell walls of old plants
Germinating seeds such as barley, where stored starch is broken down
questions.x: In germinating cereal seeds, amylase breaks starch into maltose, which is why malt is made from sprouting barley. Milk contains lactose and sugarcane stores sucrose.

questions.q: In a eukaryotic cell, most RNA is made (transcribed) in the:
questions.x: RNA is transcribed from DNA, and almost all of the DNA of a eukaryotic cell is in the nucleus. The RNA then moves out to the cytoplasm through nuclear pores.

questions.q: Adenine joined to ribose, without any phosphate group, is called:
questions.x: A base plus a sugar is a nucleoside; adenine plus ribose is adenosine. Adenylic acid (AMP) and ATP contain phosphate, and deoxyadenosine has deoxyribose.

questions.q: In a water molecule, the charges are distributed so that:
o: The oxygen atom is partly positive and each hydrogen atom is partly negative
The oxygen atom is partly negative and each hydrogen atom is partly positive
All three atoms carry equal positive charges
The molecule has no charge on any atom
questions.x: Oxygen pulls the shared electrons towards itself, so it carries a partial negative charge (δ−) and the hydrogens a partial positive charge (δ+). This uneven charge makes water polar.

questions.q: The layer of water molecules that clusters around a dissolved ion or polar molecule is called a:
questions.x: Polar water molecules surround each dissolved particle, forming a hydration shell that keeps it in solution. A micelle and a hydrophobic core form from non-polar molecules avoiding water.

questions.q: Two proteins contain the same number of amino acids and the same proportions of each kind, yet they have different shapes and functions. This is possible because they differ in:
o: The type of bond joining their amino acids
The elements present in their amino acids
The number of peptide bonds in each chain
The order (sequence) of their amino acids
questions.x: The same amino acids can be arranged in many different orders, and the sequence decides how the chain folds. The bonds (peptide), elements and number of bonds would be the same.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the roles of starch and cellulose in a plant?
o: Both are food reserves that the plant breaks down at night
Cellulose is the food reserve and starch strengthens the cell wall
Both are found only in the cell wall
Starch is a food reserve that can be broken down, while cellulose is a structural material of the cell wall
questions.x: Starch is stored in plastids and hydrolysed to glucose when needed. Cellulose forms strong fibres in the cell wall and is not used as a food reserve.

questions.q: A plant cell is placed in a concentrated salt solution. It loses water and its cytoplasm shrinks away from the cell wall. This is called:
questions.x: Water leaves the vacuole by osmosis, so the protoplast pulls away from the rigid wall: plasmolysis. Haemolysis is the bursting of red cells, and crenation is the shrinking of an animal cell, which has no wall.

questions.q: The basal body found at the base of each cilium or flagellum is similar in structure to a:
questions.x: A basal body, like a centriole, is a cylinder of nine microtubule triplets; in fact basal bodies arise from centrioles.

questions.q: The diploid number of chromosomes in the fruit fly Drosophila melanogaster is:
questions.x: Drosophila has 8 chromosomes (4 pairs) in its body cells, which makes it a useful organism for genetics. Humans have 46.

questions.q: Genes that lie close together on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together. This is called:
questions.x: Linked genes travel together because they are on one chromosome. Independent assortment applies to genes on different chromosomes.

questions.q: A gene is best described as:
o: A segment of DNA that codes for a particular protein or trait
questions.x: A gene is a stretch of DNA at a definite place on a chromosome; each chromosome carries many genes.

questions.q: A frog whose brain has been destroyed still pulls its leg away when the foot is pinched. This shows that reflexes integrated in the spinal cord:
o: Can occur without the brain taking part
Must first be learned through training
Use cranial nerves for their pathways
Need the animal to be conscious
questions.x: With the brain destroyed, only the spinal cord can link the sensory and motor neurons, yet the leg still withdraws. So spinal reflexes are organised in the spinal cord and need no brain or consciousness; they use spinal nerves.

questions.q: To keep the body balanced, the cerebellum receives impulses from the:
o: Inner ear and stretch receptors in muscles and joints
Pain receptors of the skin only
questions.x: The cerebellum uses information from the balance organs of the inner ear and from receptors in muscles and joints about body position. The cochlea is concerned with hearing, not balance.

questions.q: Which component of a spinal reflex arc is NOT part of the nervous system?
questions.x: The effector is a muscle (or gland) that carries out the response; it is not nervous tissue. The sensory, inter- and motor neurons are all parts of the nervous system.

questions.q: A typical neuron has:
o: One axon and one or more dendrites
Many axons and a single dendrite
Two axons joined at the cell body
questions.x: A typical neuron has a single axon carrying impulses away from the cell body and one or more dendrites carrying them towards it.

questions.q: In the reflex in which food on the tongue causes saliva to flow, the receptors are the:
o: Taste receptors in the taste buds
Stretch receptors in the jaw muscles
questions.x: Chemicals in the food stimulate the taste receptors (chemoreceptors) of the taste buds, which start the impulse. The salivary glands are the effectors, and motor neurons carry the outgoing impulse.

questions.q: The minimum strength of a stimulus that can make a receptor set up nerve impulses is called its:
questions.x: A stimulus must reach the threshold strength before nerve impulses are produced. Weaker stimuli produce no impulse.

questions.q: At its far end, the axon divides into fine terminal branches. Each branch ends in a swelling called the:
questions.x: Axon terminals end in synaptic knobs (terminal buttons) that hold vesicles of neurotransmitter. The axon hillock is at the start of the axon, not its end.

questions.q: Which statement about the cerebellum is correct?
o: It belongs to the hindbrain, has a folded grey cortex, and is not part of the brainstem
It is part of the brainstem, lying between the midbrain and the pons
It belongs to the forebrain and is joined to the cerebrum by the corpus callosum
It has white matter on the outside and grey matter inside
questions.x: The cerebellum is a hindbrain part behind the pons and medulla, with a folded grey cortex over white matter. The brainstem is only the midbrain, pons and medulla.

questions.q: Using the rule that the rate of an enzyme reaction doubles for each 10 °C rise, a reaction going at 5 units at 10 °C will go at about how many units at 30 °C (still below the optimum)?
questions.x: From 10 to 20 °C the rate doubles to 10 units, and from 20 to 30 °C it doubles again to 20 units.

questions.q: Koshland's model is called 'induced fit' because:
o: The enzyme causes the substrate to be made
Heat causes the enzyme to fit the substrate
The cofactor causes the enzyme to be made
Binding of the substrate causes a change in the shape of the active site
questions.x: In this model the active site is flexible; the substrate 'induces' the site to mould itself more closely around it.

questions.q: An enzyme can make a reaction go faster in several ways. Which of these is NOT one of them?
o: Bringing reacting molecules close together in the right orientation
Supplying energy to the substrate molecules
Providing a suitable chemical environment at the active site
questions.x: Enzymes lower activation energy by positioning, straining and providing a favourable environment; they do not supply energy.

questions.q: Because enzymes are proteins, the information needed to make each enzyme is carried by:
o: A gene in the cell's DNA
questions.x: A gene codes for the amino acid sequence of the enzyme's polypeptide, which folds into its shape and active site.

questions.q: Stromatolites, some of the oldest fossil evidence of life, are layered rock structures formed by:
o: Roots of the first land plants
questions.x: Stromatolites form when mats of cyanobacteria trap and bind layers of sediment. Fossil stromatolites over 3 billion years old show that photosynthetic prokaryotes existed very early.

questions.q: Supporters of Lamarck argued that Weismann's mouse-tail experiment was not a fair test of Lamarck's theory. Their reason was that:
o: Cutting off a tail is an injury, not a change caused by use or disuse in response to need
Weismann used too many generations of mice
Mice do not normally have tails
Weismann cut the tails only of female mice
questions.x: Lamarck spoke of changes produced by an animal's own use or disuse of organs. A tail cut by a scientist is an accidental injury, so critics said it did not test that idea; still, the experiment did show body changes are not inherited.

questions.q: When phospholipids are placed in water, they spontaneously form:
o: Small vesicles bounded by a lipid bilayer
questions.x: Phospholipids arrange themselves into bilayer vesicles in water. This shows how a membrane-like boundary could have formed around early protocells without enzymes.

questions.q: Darwin summed up evolution as the gradual change of species from their ancestors and called it:
questions.x: Darwin used the phrase 'descent with modification': species descend from common ancestors and change gradually through natural selection.

questions.q: If gonorrhoea is not treated in a man, the infection can spread to the epididymis and cause:
questions.x: Spread of Neisseria gonorrhoeae to the epididymis can cause inflammation and scarring that blocks sperm passage, leading to sterility.

questions.q: The two main hormones secreted by the human ovaries are:
questions.x: The ovaries secrete oestrogen (mainly from the follicle) and progesterone (mainly from the corpus luteum). FSH and LH come from the anterior pituitary.

questions.q: A patient with repeated outbreaks of genital herpes is prescribed acyclovir. What can this antiviral drug achieve?
o: Complete removal of the virus after a single dose
Fewer and shorter outbreaks, though the virus stays in the body
Permanent immunity against all sexually transmitted diseases
Killing the bacteria that cause the blisters
questions.x: Antiviral drugs such as acyclovir shorten and reduce outbreaks, but the virus stays latent in nerve cells for life. Penicillin acts only on bacteria.

questions.q: The first cervical vertebra, which carries the skull and allows the nodding movement, is the:
questions.x: The atlas (first cervical vertebra) supports the skull and lets the head nod. The axis is the second cervical vertebra, around which the atlas turns.

questions.q: The glycogen granules found in the sarcoplasm of skeletal muscle fibres serve as:
o: Binding sites for calcium ions during contraction
The protein that forms the thick filaments
A store of fuel that can be broken down to make ATP
questions.x: Glycogen is stored carbohydrate; it is broken down to glucose, which is respired to make ATP for contraction. Calcium is bound by troponin, and acetylcholine receptors lie on the sarcolemma.

questions.q: According to the sliding filament theory, when a sarcomere contracts the actin and myosin filaments themselves:
questions.x: The filaments do not shorten; they slide past one another so that their overlap increases. The sarcomere shortens even though each filament keeps its length.

questions.q: Which feature lets bone, but not cartilage, bear heavy loads without bending?
o: A matrix hardened by calcium phosphate
questions.x: Mineral salts, mainly calcium phosphate, make bone matrix hard and rigid. Chondrin, elastic fibres and perichondrium are features of cartilage.

questions.q: The M line runs across the middle of which band of a sarcomere?
o: Overlap zone of the I band
questions.x: The M line lies at the centre of the A band, inside the H zone, where it holds the thick filaments together. The Z line, not the M line, lies in the middle of the I band.

questions.q: During an asthma attack, the airways narrow because of contraction of:
o: Smooth muscle in the walls of the bronchioles
questions.x: The bronchioles have smooth muscle in their walls; its contraction narrows the airways. The diaphragm and intercostals are skeletal breathing muscles that do not line the airways.

questions.q: Which order ranks the three muscle types from the FASTEST to the SLOWEST speed of contraction?
questions.x: Skeletal muscle contracts fastest, cardiac muscle at an intermediate speed, and smooth muscle slowest, though smooth muscle can stay contracted for a long time.

questions.q: A drug that relaxes smooth muscle would most directly help to:
o: Increase the strength of the biceps
Ease painful spasms of the intestinal wall
questions.x: The intestinal wall is smooth muscle, so relaxing smooth muscle eases its spasms. The heart is cardiac muscle and the biceps and leg muscles are skeletal.

questions.q: Without crossing over, a coupling dihybrid (AB/ab) makes two kinds of gametes. With crossing over between the genes, it can make:
questions.x: Crossing over adds the two recombinant gametes, Ab and aB, to the parental AB and ab, giving four kinds in all.

questions.q: Which pair of parents can produce offspring that are half round-seeded and half wrinkled-seeded? (Round, R, is dominant.)
questions.x: Rr × rr gives 1 Rr : 1 rr, that is half round and half wrinkled. Two heterozygotes give 3 : 1, and any cross with a homozygous round parent gives only round offspring.

questions.q: Mendel's work was rediscovered in 1900 by:
questions.x: In 1900 Carl Correns, Hugo de Vries and Erich von Tschermak independently rediscovered Mendel's laws. Morgan and his students later worked on Drosophila linkage.

questions.q: Genes A, B and C lie close together on one chromosome and are completely linked (ABC/abc). How many kinds of gametes form, compared with the number if the genes were on different chromosomes?
questions.x: With complete linkage only the parental chromosomes ABC and abc go into gametes. Three independently assorting genes would give 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 kinds.

questions.q: Two parents with normal vision have a colour-blind son and a daughter with normal vision. The daughter marries a man with normal vision. What is the probability that her first child is a colour-blind son?
questions.x: The mother must be a carrier, so the daughter has a 1/2 chance of being a carrier. If she is, the chance of a colour-blind son is 1/4. So 1/2 × 1/4 = 1/8.

questions.q: In a test cross of a linked dihybrid with aabb, the percentage of recombinant offspring equals the percentage of:
o: Recombinant gametes formed by the aabb parent
Recombinant gametes formed by the dihybrid parent
Meiotic cells with a chiasma anywhere
Parental gametes formed by the dihybrid
questions.x: The aabb parent gives only ab gametes, so each offspring shows the gamete of the dihybrid. Recombinant offspring therefore reflect its recombinant gametes.

questions.q: An XᴴXʰ mother and an XᴴY father have a daughter. She later marries a man with hemophilia. The chance that her first baby is hemophilic is:
questions.x: The daughter has a 1/2 chance of being a carrier. If she is, with a hemophilic husband half of all her children are affected: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

questions.q: Two genes lie very close together on the same chromosome. They will be:
o: Separated by crossing over in every meiosis
questions.x: The chance of a crossover between two loci depends on the distance between them, so very close genes are seldom separated and are strongly linked.

questions.q: The tricuspid and bicuspid valves are together called the:
questions.x: Both valves lie between an atrium and a ventricle, so they are the atrioventricular (AV) valves. Semilunar valves guard the aorta and pulmonary trunk.

questions.q: In a cross-section, a blood vessel has a thin wall and a wide, irregular, partly collapsed lumen. The vessel is:
questions.x: Veins have thin walls with little muscle and elastic tissue, so they collapse when empty. Arteries keep a round lumen, and capillaries are microscopic tubes.

questions.q: The pulmonary circulation begins in one chamber of the heart and ends in another. These chambers are the:
questions.x: Blood leaves the right ventricle in the pulmonary trunk, passes through the lungs and returns in the pulmonary veins to the left atrium. The systemic circulation runs from left ventricle to right atrium.

questions.q: Besides its role after birth, the spleen in the fetus also:
questions.x: Before birth the spleen is one of the sites where red blood cells are made. After birth this job passes to the red bone marrow.

questions.q: A person has recovered from an infection with antigen X. Months later she meets antigen Y for the first time. Her response to Y will be:
o: A secondary response, because she already has memory cells
A primary response, because memory cells for X do not recognise Y
No response, because her lymphocytes are used up
Immediate, because antibodies against X also bind Y
questions.x: Memory cells and antibodies are specific to the antigen that made them. Antigen Y needs its own clones to be selected, so the response is a slow primary one.

questions.q: For an organ transplant, a close relative is often preferred as donor because relatives are more likely to have:
o: Similar tissue antigens on their cells
No antigens on their cells at all
questions.x: Rejection happens when the recipient's T cells recognise foreign tissue antigens. Relatives share more genes, so their tissue antigens are more alike and rejection is less likely.

questions.q: The immune system tells 'self' from 'non-self' mainly by recognising:
o: Molecules (antigens) on the surfaces of cells
The number of nuclei in the cells
questions.x: Body cells carry their own surface molecules that the immune system tolerates. Foreign cells and pathogens carry different surface antigens that lymphocytes recognise.

questions.q: A heavy smoker's blood test shows raised carboxyhaemoglobin and a red blood cell count above normal. The raised red cell count is best explained as:
o: The body's response to reduced oxygen delivery to the tissues
A direct effect of tar on the bone marrow making it cancerous
Loss of plasma water through the lungs
Destruction of red cells by nicotine
questions.x: Because carbon monoxide reduces oxygen carriage, the tissues receive less oxygen; the kidneys respond by releasing more erythropoietin, which increases red cell production. Destruction of red cells would lower the count.

questions.q: A long-term smoker begins to cough up blood-streaked mucus and is losing weight. Doctors are most concerned that he may have:
questions.x: Coughing up blood with weight loss in a long-term smoker is a warning sign of lung cancer, which must be investigated. A cold or hay fever does not usually cause bloody sputum and weight loss.

questions.q: Nicotine raises the heart rate partly by stimulating the release of:
questions.x: Nicotine stimulates the adrenal glands to release adrenaline, which speeds the heart and narrows blood vessels. Insulin, thyroxine and ADH are not the hormones responsible for this quick effect.

questions.q: In infants, an enzyme in gastric juice curdles milk so that it stays longer in the stomach for protein digestion. This enzyme is:
questions.x: Rennin converts soluble milk protein (caseinogen) into insoluble curd (casein), so pepsin has time to act. Renin, spelt with one n, is a kidney enzyme that helps control blood pressure.

questions.q: A child's 20 milk teeth are later replaced by 32 permanent teeth. Which permanent teeth grow without any milk tooth before them?
questions.x: The milk set has 8 incisors, 4 canines and 8 molars. Permanent incisors and canines replace their milk forms and the premolars replace the milk molars, so the 12 permanent molars have no milk predecessors.

questions.q: The salivary glands that lie in the floor of the mouth directly under the tongue are the:
questions.x: 'Sublingual' means under the tongue. The parotids lie in front of the ears and the submandibular glands lie along the inner side of the lower jaw; tonsils are lymphoid tissue, not salivary glands.

questions.q: The yellow colour of normal urine is due to the pigment:
questions.x: Urochrome, derived from the breakdown of haemoglobin, gives urine its yellow colour. Bilirubin goes mainly into bile; its presence in urine suggests jaundice.

questions.q: ADH is injected into a person who is already well hydrated. Which effect on the blood is expected?
o: Its water content falls and its osmotic concentration rises
No change, because ADH acts only on urine
Its water content rises and its osmotic concentration falls
questions.x: ADH makes the collecting ducts reabsorb more water even though the body does not need it. That extra water dilutes the blood, lowering its osmotic concentration below normal.

questions.q: Which statement about the two types of nephron in the human kidney is correct?
o: Most are juxtamedullary nephrons with long loops
There are equal numbers of each type
Cortical nephrons have no loop of Henle at all
Most are cortical nephrons; only a minority are juxtamedullary
questions.x: The large majority of human nephrons are cortical, with short loops; a smaller share are juxtamedullary, with long loops reaching deep into the medulla. Cortical nephrons still have a short loop.

questions.q: Camels in the desert let their body temperature rise by several degrees during the day and lose the stored heat in the cool night. This mainly helps them to:
o: Save water that would otherwise be lost in sweat
questions.x: By tolerating a higher body temperature by day, the camel needs to sweat far less, conserving scarce water.

questions.q: Why is a patient with severe kidney failure often told to drink only limited amounts of fluid?
o: The kidneys cannot remove the extra water, so it builds up in the body
questions.x: Without working kidneys, excess water is not excreted; it accumulates, causing swelling, high blood pressure and even fluid in the lungs.

questions.q: A patient with kidney failure is often advised to limit dietary protein because:
o: Protein turns into glucose in the urine
Breakdown of excess protein produces urea, which the kidneys cannot remove well
questions.x: Excess amino acids are deaminated and their nitrogen is turned into urea. Less protein means less urea for the failing kidneys to clear.

questions.q: Which measure helps prevent chronic kidney failure in a person with diabetes?
o: Keeping blood glucose and blood pressure well controlled
Drinking as little water as possible
questions.x: Diabetes and high blood pressure are the main causes of chronic kidney failure, so controlling both protects the glomeruli.

questions.q: Peritubular capillaries form a network wrapped closely around the tubules along their length. This arrangement suits them for:
o: Forcing fluid into the tubule under high pressure
Taking up reabsorbed substances and supplying substances for secretion all along the tubule
Storing urine before it reaches the pelvis
questions.x: Close contact along the whole tubule lets reabsorbed water and solutes enter the blood wherever they leave the tubule, and lets H+, K+ and drugs be delivered for secretion. Their pressure is low, so they do not filter.

questions.q: Within the kidney, stones are most often found in the:
o: Renal pelvis and calyces, where urine collects
questions.x: Stones build up where urine collects and salts can crystallise, in the calyces and renal pelvis, and may then move into the ureter.

questions.q: Louis Pasteur developed attenuated vaccines, including one against:
questions.x: Pasteur weakened (attenuated) pathogens in the laboratory and produced vaccines against chicken cholera, anthrax and rabies. The smallpox vaccine came from Jenner, and polio and measles vaccines came in the twentieth century.

questions.q: Haemophilia B is treated with recombinant:
questions.x: Haemophilia B results from a lack of clotting factor IX, whereas haemophilia A results from lack of factor VIII. Both can be treated with the correct recombinant clotting factor.

questions.q: The name of the restriction enzyme EcoRI shows that it was first isolated from:
questions.x: Restriction enzymes are named after the bacterium they come from: 'Eco' stands for Escherichia coli, 'R' for the strain and 'I' because it was the first enzyme found in that strain.

questions.q: Potassium chlorate decomposes on heating: 2KClO₃ → 2KCl + 3O₂. What mass of oxygen is released by 0.2 mol of KClO₃? (O = 16)
questions.x: 0.2 mol KClO₃ gives 0.2 × 3/2 = 0.3 mol O₂; mass = 0.3 × 32 = 9.6 g. 6.4 g assumes a 1 : 1 ratio; 4.8 g uses 16 instead of 32 for O₂.

questions.q: For CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂, heating 20 g of calcium carbonate gives 3.36 dm³ of CO₂ at STP. What is the percentage yield of CO₂? (CaCO₃ = 100 g mol⁻¹)
questions.x: 20 g = 0.2 mol CaCO₃, so the theoretical CO₂ = 0.2 × 22.4 = 4.48 dm³. Yield = 3.36/4.48 × 100 = 75%.

questions.q: The total number of electrons in p orbitals of an argon atom (Z = 18) is:
questions.x: Ar is 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶. The p electrons are 2p⁶ + 3p⁶ = 12.

questions.q: The number of sub-levels (subshells) in the fourth principal energy level (n = 4) is:
questions.x: Shell n contains n sub-levels: n = 4 has 4s, 4p, 4d and 4f. Sixteen is its number of orbitals and 32 its maximum number of electrons.

questions.q: In an electric field, positive rays are deflected:
questions.x: Positive rays are made of positively charged ions, so they are attracted towards the negative plate. Cathode rays bend the other way, towards the positive plate.

questions.q: The kinetic molecular theory assumes there are no forces between gas molecules except during collisions. So, between two collisions, the speed of a molecule:
questions.x: With no force acting on it between collisions, a molecule moves in a straight line at constant speed. Its speed changes only when it collides with another molecule or a wall.

questions.q: Two flasks at the same temperature contain 1 mol of helium and 2 mol of neon. Compared with the helium, the total kinetic energy of the neon molecules is:
questions.x: Average kinetic energy per molecule depends only on temperature, so it is the same for both gases. Neon has twice as many molecules, so its total kinetic energy is twice as large; molar mass does not matter.

questions.q: A gas occupies 3 dm³ at 760 mm Hg. At constant temperature, it is compressed until the pressure is 1140 mm Hg. Its new volume is:
questions.x: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂: V₂ = 760 × 3/1140 = 2 dm³. The 4.5 dm³ value comes from inverting the pressure ratio.

questions.q: A closed flask holds water and its vapour at equilibrium at 25 °C. More water at 25 °C is added, leaving some space above it. The vapour pressure:
questions.x: Vapour pressure depends only on the nature of the liquid and the temperature, not on the amount of liquid present.

questions.q: For most substances the solid is denser than the liquid. Water is unusual because its solid form:
o: Has its molecules packed more closely than in the liquid
Contains no hydrogen bonds at all
Has an open hydrogen-bonded structure with more empty space than the liquid
Is made of ions instead of molecules
questions.x: In ice, hydrogen bonds hold the molecules in an open arrangement with large spaces, so ice takes up more volume than the same mass of liquid water.

questions.q: Crystals whose axial lengths are all different (a ≠ b ≠ c) but whose axes are mutually perpendicular are classed as:
questions.x: Unequal edges with all angles 90° is orthorhombic. Triclinic has no angle equal to 90°, and monoclinic has one angle not equal to 90°.

questions.q: Grey tin and white tin are two crystalline forms of the same element tin. This type of polymorphism shown by an element is called:
questions.x: Polymorphism in an element is called allotropy; grey and white tin are allotropes. Isomorphism involves different substances.

questions.q: Which mixture, after reaction in water, gives a buffer solution?
questions.x: 0.1 mol NaOH turns half the acid into CH₃COONa, leaving 0.1 mol CH₃COOH with 0.1 mol CH₃COO⁻: a buffer. Equal moles of acid and NaOH leave only salt; HCl and NaOH give no weak acid.

questions.q: The Kc expression for 2NO₂(g) ⇌ N₂O₄(g) is:
questions.x: Kc = products over reactants, each raised to its coefficient: [N₂O₄]/[NO₂]². Coefficients are powers, not multipliers.

questions.q: For rate = k[X], the rate is 0.01 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹ when [X] = 0.5 mol dm⁻³. The temperature is raised so that k becomes three times as large, and [X] is lowered to 0.25 mol dm⁻³. The new rate is:
questions.x: New rate = 0.01 × 3 (larger k) × ½ (half the concentration) = 0.015 mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹.

questions.q: Which statement about an elementary (single-step) reaction is correct?
o: It always involves more than three colliding molecules
It always has an order of zero
It must pass through at least one intermediate
Its order equals its molecularity, so its rate equation follows from its equation
questions.x: For a single elementary step, the powers in the rate equation are the numbers of each particle in that step. An elementary step has no intermediate; it passes only through an activated complex.

questions.q: A first-order reaction, rate = k[X], has a rate of 3.0 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹ when [X] = 0.015 mol dm⁻³. The value of k is:
questions.x: k = rate/[X] = 3.0 × 10⁻⁴ / 1.5 × 10⁻² = 2 × 10⁻² s⁻¹. Multiplying instead of dividing gives 4.5 × 10⁻⁶.

questions.q: The unit of molar heat capacity is:
questions.x: Molar heat capacity is energy per mole per kelvin. J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ is the unit of specific heat capacity and J K⁻¹ that of heat capacity.

questions.q: ΔHf values (kJ mol⁻¹): H₂O₂(l) −188, H₂O(l) −286. What is ΔH for 2H₂O₂(l) → 2H₂O(l) + O₂(g)?
questions.x: ΔH = ΣΔHf(products) − ΣΔHf(reactants) = 2(−286) − 2(−188) = −572 + 376 = −196 kJ. ΔHf of O₂ is zero.

questions.q: Which of these changes is exothermic?
questions.x: A chlorine atom releases energy when it gains an electron (electron affinity). Ionisation, melting and sublimation all absorb energy.

questions.q: Which of the following changes is a reduction?
questions.x: Nitrogen falls from +5 in NO₃⁻ to −3 in NH₄⁺, a decrease in oxidation number. The other three are increases (oxidations).

questions.q: SO₂ and H₂O are both bent molecules. Which statement about them is correct?
o: Both central atoms have two lone pairs, so their bond angles are equal
Sulphur in SO₂ has two lone pairs, so its angle is smaller than in water
Sulphur in SO₂ has one lone pair, while oxygen in H₂O has two, so the angle in water is smaller
Neither central atom has a lone pair; they are bent because of their double bonds
questions.x: In SO₂ sulphur has two bonding regions and one lone pair (angle close to 120°). In H₂O oxygen has two lone pairs, which squeeze the angle to 104.5°.

questions.q: The hybridisation of the carbon atom in methanal (formaldehyde), HCHO, is:
questions.x: Carbon forms three σ bonds (two C–H, one C–O) and one π bond with oxygen, so it uses three sp² hybrid orbitals and one unhybridised p orbital.

questions.q: Sodium chloride melts at 801 °C, but hydrogen chloride is a gas at room temperature. The best explanation is that:
o: NaCl has a lattice of ions held by strong electrostatic forces, while HCl has separate molecules held by weak intermolecular forces
The H–Cl covalent bond is weaker than the attractions in NaCl
Chlorine is more electronegative in NaCl than in HCl
questions.x: Melting NaCl means breaking the strong forces between all the ions. Boiling HCl only separates polar molecules held by weak dipole forces; the H–Cl bond itself is not broken.

questions.q: Silicon reacts with warm sodium hydroxide solution: Si + 2NaOH + H₂O → Na₂SiO₃ + 2H₂. Which statement is correct?
o: Silicon is oxidised from 0 to +4 and hydrogen is released
Oxygen is given off and silicon is unchanged
It is a neutralisation with no change in oxidation number
questions.x: Si goes from 0 to +4 in Na₂SiO₃, and hydrogen from +1 to 0 in H₂, so this is a redox reaction typical of a non-metal with alkali.

questions.q: The lanthanides and actinides together make up the:
questions.x: In the lanthanides and actinides the differentiating electron enters 4f or 5f orbitals, so they form the f-block.

questions.q: Which gaseous ion is diamagnetic?
questions.x: Sc³⁺ is [Ar] 3d⁰ with no unpaired electrons, so it is diamagnetic. Ti³⁺ (3d¹), V³⁺ (3d²) and Cr³⁺ (3d³) all have unpaired electrons and are paramagnetic.

questions.q: Which compound contains a carbonyl group but is NOT an aldehyde?
questions.x: Butanone has its C=O between two carbon atoms, so it is a ketone. The other three have the –CHO group of aldehydes.

questions.q: Phenol, C₆H₅OH, and cyclohexanol, C₆H₁₁OH, both contain a six-carbon ring. They differ in classification because:
o: Phenol is alicyclic, while cyclohexanol is aromatic
Phenol is heterocyclic, while cyclohexanol is homocyclic
Phenol is open-chain, while cyclohexanol is closed-chain
Phenol is aromatic, while cyclohexanol is alicyclic
questions.x: Phenol's ring is a benzene ring, so it is aromatic. Cyclohexanol's ring is saturated, like cyclohexane, so it is alicyclic. Neither ring contains a heteroatom.

questions.q: CH₂=CHCl is commonly called vinyl chloride. Its IUPAC name is:
questions.x: It is ethene with one H replaced by Cl, so it is chloroethene. Chloroethane, CH₃CH₂Cl, has no double bond.

questions.q: Free rotation about the C=C bond in ethene is not possible because:
o: Rotation would destroy the sideways overlap of the p orbitals forming the π bond
The σ bond between the carbons is too short
The hydrogen atoms repel each other strongly
The carbon atoms are sp³ hybridised
questions.x: The π bond needs the two p orbitals to stay parallel. Twisting one carbon relative to the other would break this overlap, so rotation is restricted.

questions.q: 5.2 g of ethyne reacts completely with ammoniacal copper(I) chloride to form copper(I) acetylide, Cu₂C₂. What mass of precipitate is formed? (C 12, H 1, Cu 63.5)
Ethene reacts with hydrogen bromide. The product is:
questions.x: HBr adds across the double bond: CH₂=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CH₂Br. 1,2-dibromoethane forms with Br₂, not HBr.

questions.q: Methane is treated with a limited amount of bromine in sunlight. The main products are:
questions.x: Bromination follows the same free-radical substitution as chlorination: CH₄ + Br₂ → CH₃Br + HBr. With little bromine, mainly one hydrogen is replaced.

questions.q: Acetylene, HC≡CH, is the simplest alkyne. Its IUPAC name is:
questions.x: The two-carbon chain is "eth-" and the triple bond gives the ending "-yne". Acetylene is its common name.

questions.q: In the chlorination of ethane, which two species can combine in a termination step to give chloroethane?
questions.x: An ethyl radical joining a chlorine radical gives C₂H₅Cl. Two ethyl radicals give butane, two chlorine radicals give Cl₂, and two methyl radicals give ethane.

questions.q: (CH₃)₃CBr is warmed with water and undergoes SN1 hydrolysis. The organic product is:
questions.x: The tertiary carbocation (CH₃)₃C⁺ is attacked by water, giving (CH₃)₃COH, 2-methylpropan-2-ol. The OH ends up on the same carbon that carried the bromine; 2-methylpropene would be an elimination product.

questions.q: The correct order of reactivity of alcohols towards Lucas reagent (forming alkyl chlorides) is:
questions.x: The C–O bond breaks most easily in tertiary alcohols, which give cloudiness at once; secondary ones take a few minutes and primary ones react only on heating.

questions.q: Compared with benzene, phenol undergoes electrophilic substitution:
o: Only in the presence of a strong Lewis acid
questions.x: The –OH group feeds electron density into the ring, activating it, so phenol reacts with electrophiles far more readily than benzene, often without a catalyst.

questions.q: Benzaldehyde, C₆H₅CHO, is less reactive than ethanal towards nucleophilic addition. The main reason is that:
o: The benzene ring donates electron density to the carbonyl carbon by resonance, reducing its positive charge
The benzene ring makes the carbonyl carbon more positive
Benzaldehyde has no hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon
Benzaldehyde has an sp³ carbonyl carbon
questions.x: Conjugation of the C=O with the ring spreads π electron density onto the carbonyl carbon, lowering its δ+ charge, so nucleophiles attack it less readily. Benzaldehyde does have an H on its carbonyl carbon.

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the reactions of aldehydes and ketones?
o: On reduction, aldehydes give secondary alcohols and ketones give primary alcohols
On reduction, aldehydes give primary alcohols and ketones give secondary alcohols
questions.x: Adding H₂ across C=O turns RCHO into RCH₂OH (primary) and RCOR′ into RCH(OH)R′ (secondary). Both classes give 2,4-DNPH precipitates and both undergo nucleophilic addition.

questions.q: Which is the correct IUPAC name for the ketone (CH₃)₂CHCOCH₃?
questions.x: The main chain has four carbons; numbering from the end nearer the C=O puts it on C-2 and the methyl on C-3. '2-Methylbutan-3-one' gives the carbonyl a higher number; 3-methylbutanal and pentan-2-one are isomers.

questions.q: Ethanoic acid reacts with magnesium ribbon. The products are:
questions.x: Like other acids, it reacts with a reactive metal: 2CH₃COOH + Mg → (CH₃COO)₂Mg + H₂.

questions.q: Glycine (Gly) and alanine (Ala) can join in either order, and an amino acid can also join to itself. How many different dipeptides can be formed from these two amino acids?
questions.x: Gly–Gly, Ala–Ala, Gly–Ala and Ala–Gly. Gly–Ala and Ala–Gly are different because the free –NH₂ and –COOH ends are on different units.

questions.q: The first synthetic dye, mauveine, was discovered by:
questions.x: W. H. Perkin made mauveine by accident while trying to make quinine, which started the synthetic dye industry. Wöhler is known for making urea.

questions.q: The scalar product of a vector P with itself, P · P, is equal to:
o: The square of the magnitude of P
questions.x: The angle between a vector and itself is 0°, so P · P = P × P × cos 0° = P². It is a scalar, not a vector.

questions.q: To solve a one-dimensional perfectly elastic collision, the relation u₁ − u₂ = v₂ − v₁ is used together with:
questions.x: The relative-speed relation replaces the kinetic energy equation. Together with m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ it gives two simple equations for the two unknown final velocities.

questions.q: Ignoring air resistance, a projectile passes the same height once while rising and once while falling. At these two points its speeds are:
questions.x: With no air resistance mechanical energy is conserved, so at equal heights the kinetic energy, and therefore the speed, is the same.

questions.q: How long after launch does a projectile reach the top of its path if it starts with an upward velocity component of 25 m s⁻¹? (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.x: At the top the vertical velocity is zero: 0 = 25 − 10t, so t = 2.5 s. 5 s is the whole time of flight on level ground.

questions.q: A stone is thrown horizontally from a cliff top. If its horizontal launch speed is doubled, its time to reach the ground (ignoring air resistance):
questions.x: The time of fall depends only on the vertical motion, which has zero initial velocity and acceleration g in both cases. The horizontal speed changes only how far the stone lands.

questions.q: The velocity of a 2 kg body increases from 3 m s⁻¹ to 8 m s⁻¹ in the same direction. The impulse acting on it is:
questions.x: Impulse = change in momentum = 2 × (8 − 3) = 10 N s. 22 N s adds the two momenta (6 + 16) instead of subtracting.

questions.q: When analysing projectile motion, the axes are usually chosen with:
o: Both axes horizontal and at right angles
The x-axis along the initial velocity and the y-axis perpendicular to it
The x-axis horizontal and the y-axis vertical, origin at the launch point
The y-axis horizontal and the x-axis along the path
questions.x: Choosing x horizontal and y vertical splits the motion into a horizontal part with no acceleration and a vertical part with acceleration g.

questions.q: Near the Earth's surface, the gravitational potential energy of a body of mass m at height h is:
questions.x: Lifting a body of weight mg through height h needs work mgh, which is stored as gravitational potential energy.

questions.q: A force vector F = (2i + 3j) N acts on a body moving with velocity vector v = (4i − 2j) m s⁻¹. The power delivered by the force is:
questions.x: P = F·v = (2)(4) + (3)(−2) = 8 − 6 = 2 W. Adding magnitudes of the products (8 + 6) gives the wrong 14 W.

questions.q: A simple pendulum swings with no air resistance. At the lowest point of its swing the bob has:
o: Maximum potential energy and zero kinetic energy
Maximum kinetic energy and minimum potential energy
Zero kinetic energy and zero potential energy
questions.x: As the bob falls to its lowest point, potential energy turns into kinetic energy, so its speed and kinetic energy are greatest there; the total energy stays constant.

questions.q: A stone on a string is whirled in a circle at a fixed angular speed. If the string is made twice as long, the linear speed of the stone:
questions.x: v = rω; with ω fixed, doubling r doubles v.

questions.q: Two liquids flow through identical pipes at the same speed. Compared with the less viscous liquid, the more viscous liquid is:
o: Equally likely to become turbulent, since viscosity has no effect
questions.x: Viscosity damps out disturbances and keeps layers moving smoothly, so a more viscous liquid stays laminar up to a higher speed.

questions.q: In the steady flow of a fluid, all fluid particles that pass through a particular fixed point:
o: Have the same velocity at every point of their path
Have velocities that change randomly with time at that point
Have the same velocity as one another at that point
questions.x: Steady flow means the velocity at each fixed point does not change with time, so every particle reaching that point has the same velocity there. A particle's velocity may still change as it moves to other points.

questions.q: In a car engine's carburettor, petrol is drawn into the air stream at a narrow throat. This happens because:
o: Air in the throat moves slowly and has a high pressure
Air moving fast through the narrow throat has a low pressure
The air in the throat is turbulent
questions.x: By continuity the air speeds up in the narrow throat, and by Bernoulli's principle its pressure drops, so the higher pressure on the petrol pushes it into the air stream.

questions.q: In a Bunsen burner, air is drawn in through holes near the base of the tube. This happens because:
o: The gas jet raises the pressure inside the tube
The holes contain a small pump
The fast jet of gas lowers the pressure around it, so outside air is pushed in
questions.x: The high-speed gas jet is at low pressure (Bernoulli's effect), so the higher atmospheric pressure outside pushes air in through the holes to mix with the gas.

questions.q: Light from two separate ordinary lamps falling on a screen does not produce a visible interference pattern. The main reason is that the lamps:
o: Are not coherent, since their phase difference changes randomly
Emit light of exactly the same frequency
questions.x: Ordinary lamps emit light in random bursts, so the phase difference between them keeps changing and any pattern shifts too fast to see. A steady pattern needs coherent sources.

questions.q: Waves from two sources reach a point with a phase difference of 2π. How much farther has one wave travelled than the other?
questions.x: A path difference of one wavelength corresponds to a phase difference of 2π. Half a wavelength would give π.

questions.q: Helium (γ = 1.67) and nitrogen (γ = 1.40) are compared at the same pressure and the same density. According to Laplace's formula, sound travels:
o: Faster in nitrogen, because its γ is smaller
Faster in helium, because its γ is larger
At the same speed in both, because P and ρ are the same
Faster in nitrogen, because its molecules are heavier
questions.x: v = √(γP/ρ); with P and ρ equal, v ∝ √γ, so the gas with the larger γ (helium) carries sound faster.

questions.q: For a mechanical wave in a given medium, the energy carried is proportional to f²A², where f is the frequency and A the amplitude. If f is doubled and A is halved, the energy carried becomes:
questions.x: New energy ∝ (2f)²(A/2)² = 4f² × A²/4 = f²A². The two changes cancel.

questions.q: The projection of a uniformly rotating point on a diameter passes through the centre of the circle. At that moment the speed of the projection is:
o: Half the speed of the rotating point
Twice the speed of the rotating point
Equal to the speed of the rotating point
questions.x: At the centre the rotating point's velocity is parallel to the diameter, so the projection moves with the full speed ωr. This is the maximum speed of the SHM.

questions.q: For a certain gas, Newton's formula gives the speed of sound as 300 m s⁻¹, while Laplace's formula gives 390 m s⁻¹. The value of γ for this gas is:
questions.x: v(Laplace)/v(Newton) = √γ, so √γ = 390/300 = 1.3 and γ = 1.3² = 1.69. Forgetting to square gives 1.30.

questions.q: In an isothermal change of an ideal gas, which quantity is zero?
o: The work done by the gas
questions.x: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature. At constant temperature ΔU = 0, so the heat supplied equals the work done by the gas.

questions.q: A metal of molar mass 50 g mol⁻¹ has a specific heat of 500 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. The heat needed to raise the temperature of 1 mol of it by 1 K is:
questions.x: 1 mol has a mass of 0.05 kg, so heat = 0.05 × 500 × 1 = 25 J. Using 50 kg instead of 0.05 kg gives 25 000 J.

questions.q: A charge of 5 nC is 2 cm from a large charged conducting plate (well away from its edges), where the field is 4 × 10⁴ N C⁻¹. The charge is moved to 4 cm from the plate. The force on it is now:
questions.x: The field of a large plate does not depend on distance, so F = qE = 5 × 10⁻⁹ × 4 × 10⁴ = 2 × 10⁻⁴ N, the same as before.

questions.q: An alpha particle (charge +2e) is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of 1000 V. Taking e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, the kinetic energy it gains is:
questions.x: K = qV = 2 × 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 1000 = 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁶ J (2000 eV). Using charge e instead of 2e gives 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁶ J.

questions.q: A large charged plate with surface charge density σ is placed in a medium of relative permittivity εr instead of vacuum. The electric field near it:
o: Is reduced by the factor εr
Is increased by the factor εr
Is reduced by the factor εr²
questions.x: In a medium ε₀ is replaced by εrε₀, so the field σ/ε₀ becomes σ/(εrε₀), smaller by a factor εr, just as Coulomb's force is reduced in a medium.

questions.q: When a battery is matched to its load for the greatest power output, how large is the circuit current in terms of emf E and internal resistance r?
questions.x: For maximum power R = r, so the total resistance is 2r and I = E/2r. E/r would be the short-circuit current.

questions.q: A uniform wire is cut into two equal halves. Compared with the original wire, the resistivity of each half is:
questions.x: Resistivity depends only on the material and temperature, not on size. Each half has half the resistance, but the same resistivity.

questions.q: Two ions with the same charge and the same speed enter a uniform magnetic field at right angles. The heavier ion moves in a circle that is:
o: Larger, because r is proportional to mass
Smaller, because r is inversely proportional to mass
The same size, because the charges are equal
Larger, because r is proportional to the square of mass
questions.x: r = mv/(qB); with q, v and B equal, r is directly proportional to m. This is how a mass spectrometer separates ions.

questions.q: An ideal transformer with turns ratio Ns : Np = 1 : 20 is connected to 220 V AC. Its secondary is connected to an 11 Ω resistor. The current in the primary is:
questions.x: Vs = 220/20 = 11 V, so Is = 11/11 = 1 A. Power is conserved, so Ip = Is × Ns/Np = 1/20 = 0.05 A.

questions.q: A magnet is pushed into a coil connected to a lamp, and the lamp glows. The electrical energy in the lamp comes from the:
o: Work done by the person against the repelling force
Energy stored in the magnet, which slowly weakens
Internal energy of the copper wire
questions.x: By Lenz's law the coil repels the magnet, so the person must do work to push it in. That work becomes electrical energy, in line with energy conservation.

questions.q: During one complete cycle of an alternating voltage, its phase changes by:
questions.x: One full cycle of an alternating quantity corresponds to a phase change of 2π rad, or 360°, after which the values repeat.

questions.q: The electronic component that lets current pass easily in one direction only, and is therefore used to convert AC into DC, is the:
questions.x: A diode conducts when forward biased and blocks current when reverse biased, so it passes only one direction of current. Capacitors, resistors and inductors do not act as one-way valves.

questions.q: Light whose photons carry 3 eV shines on a surface with a 2 eV work function. Doubling the light's frequency changes the energy of the fastest ejected electrons to:
questions.x: Originally KEmax = 3 − 2 = 1 eV. Doubling frequency gives 6 eV photons, so KEmax = 6 − 2 = 4 eV, which is 4 times the original, not simply double.

questions.q: In Bohr's model, the angular momentum of the electron in the nth allowed orbit is:
questions.x: Bohr's quantisation condition is mvr = nh/2π, so only orbits with angular momentum a whole multiple of h/2π are allowed.

questions.q: The nucleus of cobalt-60, ⁶⁰₂₇Co, contains how many neutrons?
questions.x: The number of neutrons is N = A − Z = 60 − 27 = 33. The 27 is the number of protons.

questions.q: The poet writes, "Time is a thief that steals our years." What idea does this line express?
o: Time quietly takes away our life and youth
Time passes more slowly as we grow old
People waste their time on useless things
Most thefts take place late at night
questions.x: The metaphor compares time to a thief: our years slip away from us without our noticing, as a thief takes things secretly. The line says nothing about time slowing down or wasting time.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: "Not until the results came out ___ how well she had done."
questions.x: 'Not until ...' at the start of a sentence causes inversion in the main clause: auxiliary + subject + verb.

questions.q: A stage play shows greedy, corrupt officials as foolish clowns so that the audience laughs and also thinks about real corruption. The play is mainly a:
questions.x: Satire uses humour and ridicule to criticise real faults in society; a tragedy is serious, an elegy mourns, and a biography tells a life story.

questions.q: A fire station burns down because its own fire alarm was faulty. This situation is an example of:
questions.x: Situational irony is when the outcome is the opposite of what we expect; a fire station is the last place we expect to burn down.

questions.q: What is the correct way to write 'the bicycle belonging to Ali'?
questions.x: A singular noun shows possession with an apostrophe and s: Ali's.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: "The hotel was dirty, the food was cold and the staff were rude. ___, it was a terrible stay."
questions.x: 'In short' introduces a summary of the points already made.

questions.q: Choose the correct pronoun: "The committee members cast ___ votes one by one."
questions.x: The antecedent 'members' is plural, so the plural pronoun 'their' is needed.

questions.q: Choose the correct spelling to fill the blank: "Keep raw meat ____ from cooked food."
questions.x: The correct spelling is 'separate', with 'a' after the 'p' and again before the 't'. 'Seperate' is a very common misspelling.

questions.q: Which group of words cannot stand on its own as a sentence?
o: The lift was not working, so we used the stairs.
We used the stairs because the lift was not working.
Because the lift was not working.
questions.x: A clause beginning with 'because' depends on a main clause and cannot stand alone. The other three each contain a complete main clause.

questions.q: The claim "All the mangoes in this crate are ripe" has been shown to be false. Which statement must be true?
o: No mango in this crate is ripe
At least one mango in this crate is not ripe
Most of the mangoes in this crate are unripe
Exactly one mango in this crate is unripe
questions.x: To make 'all are ripe' false, only one unripe mango is needed. It does not follow that none, most or exactly one are unripe.

questions.q: A doctor claims: "Every patient who took the new tablet recovered." Which observation would prove the claim false?
o: A patient who did not take the tablet recovered
Some patients refused to take the tablet
A patient who took the new tablet did not recover
The tablet was more costly than other tablets
questions.x: An 'every' claim is disproved by one case where the condition holds but the result does not. Patients who did not take the tablet are outside the claim.

questions.q: Find the next number: 1, 3, 7, 13, 21, ?
questions.x: The differences are 2, 4, 6, 8, so the next difference is 10: 21 + 10 = 31.

questions.q: Usman walks 2 km west, turns left and walks 5 km, then turns left again and walks 14 km. Where is he now from his starting point?
questions.x: Left from west is south (5 km), left from south is east (14 km). He ends 12 km east and 5 km south of the start; the distance is the square root of 144 + 25 = 13 km, towards the south-east.

questions.q: Statements: All nurses in this ward are trained in first aid. Sara is a nurse in this ward. Which conclusion follows?
o: Everyone trained in first aid is a nurse
Sara is not trained in first aid
Sara is trained in first aid
Some nurses in this ward are not trained in first aid
questions.x: Sara belongs to the group 'nurses in this ward', and every member of that group is trained in first aid, so Sara is too. The reverse statement does not follow.

questions.q: Four chairs in a line are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right. Usman takes chair 1. Ali's chair is neither of the end chairs, and Bilal's is the chair just to Ali's right. Hamza is not beside Usman. Who takes chair 4?
questions.x: Ali and Bilal take chairs 2-3 or 3-4. If they took 3-4, Hamza would be in chair 2 beside Usman, which is not allowed. So Ali is 2, Bilal 3 and Hamza 4.

questions.q: Statement: Many buyers complain that a shop's weighing scale shows more weight than it actually gives. Courses of action: I. All the shops in the market should be closed. II. The weights and measures department should check the shop's scale. Which course(s) of action follow?
questions.x: Checking the scale deals with the complaint about one shop. Closing every shop in the market punishes people who did nothing wrong.

questions.q: Statement I: Far more people than usual visited the city's parks on Sunday. Statement II: Sunday was a pleasant, sunny day after a week of rain. Which of the following is correct?
o: Statement I is the cause and statement II is its effect
Both statements are effects of some common cause
Statement II is the cause and statement I is its effect
Both statements are effects of independent causes
questions.x: Fine weather after days of rain encourages people to go out. The weather is the cause of the larger crowds, even though it is stated second.

questions.q: Sana revised for only one day before her exam. On the way to the exam she saw a crow, and later she blamed the crow for her poor result. What is the valid explanation of her result?
o: The crow brought her bad luck
Too little revision, not the crow, explains her poor result
Exams are always harder on days when crows are seen
Her result was decided before she sat the exam
questions.x: Preparation affects exam marks directly, and she did very little. A bird seen on the way has no link to her answers.
